title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description:
You are given two integer arrays, `preorder` and `inorder`, which are the preorder and inorder traversals of the same binary tree. All values are distinct.

Rebuild the tree and return its root.

examples.explanation: 3 is first in preorder so it is the root. In inorder, everything before 3 ([9]) is the left subtree and everything after ([15,20,7]) is the right subtree.

constraints: All values are unique and the traversals describe the same tree.
hints: The first element of preorder is always the root of the current subtree.
Find that root in inorder: elements to its left form the left subtree, elements to its right form the right subtree.
Slicing arrays and calling index() each time is O(n^2). Store value -> inorder index in a hash map and recurse on index ranges with a single moving preorder pointer.
signature: def buildTree(self, preorder: List[int], inorder: List[int]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
approach:
**Preorder tells you the root; inorder tells you how many nodes go left of it.** The first unused preorder value is the root of the current subtree. Its position `mid` in inorder splits the current inorder range into the left subtree `[lo, mid-1]` and the right subtree `[mid+1, hi]`. Because preorder lists the entire left subtree before the right one, consuming preorder values with a single forward pointer while recursing left-then-right hands every subtree exactly its own root.

**Making it linear:** a hash map from value to inorder index replaces the O(n) `index()` lookup, and passing index bounds instead of slicing avoids copying. The result is O(n) time and O(n) space. The 3000-node chain test is where the slicing version turns quadratic.

**Common mistakes:** slicing `preorder[1:mid+1]` and `inorder[:mid]` at every level (O(n^2) in both time and memory); building the right subtree before the left while sharing the preorder pointer; off-by-one on the inorder bounds.

**Interview follow-ups:** inorder + postorder (same idea, consume postorder from the back and build right first); preorder + postorder (not unique in general, show why); do it iteratively with a stack; what if values are not unique (the reconstruction is ambiguous).

complexity.space: O(n) for the index map plus O(h) recursion
